title: Are my game play "juicy" enough to catch attention?
author: pennystudio
selftext:
I really appreciate the feedbacks and advices I received from the last post on how to market a game. And I am slowly trying to implement some of them. 

One advice is to create and post some contents about the game play. So here are a sample of two to get a feel, are these "juicy" enough? 

I heard advices that it doesn't matter how good the game it is graphically but if the game mechanics is not fun enough it still doesn't matter. But on the other hand, even if the game mechanics is fun, without a good graphic to attract players there still won't be anyone to discover the fun mechanics. That catch-22 almost requires you to ship a pretty polish game. 

I think I am far away from that but would appreciate any feedback.

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body: It doesn't look awful but I also still don't really understand the game by watching it. Is it a board game?

replies.author: Cool-Chemical-5629
replies.body: It looks like some sort of VERY overhauled take on Monopoly game. So yes, a board game indeed. Judging by the look of controls, width and height of the viewport, I guess it is probably a mobile game. It does look like a fun Monopoly game though, like I'd like to play it, even on my PC if it's ever released there.

replies.author: pennystudio
replies.body: Yes it's a monopoly style dice roller board game.

comments.author: PSloVR
comments.body: Overall art style looks looks fairly cohesive so that's good.  The slight pause during the character walks stands out and should be fixed.  Same with the character walking over the bridge and their distance to the floor not matching the height change of the bridge.  The menus themselves also need a visual overhaul they look bad.

replies.author: pennystudio
replies.body: Very good feedback. Making it overall smoother seems to be the right way to go. That's concrete actionable.

comments.author: miomao10
comments.body: Seems confusing, slow, and I don’t like how the screen moves something is off

comments.author: fued
comments.body:
not great honestly, heres a list of feedback

\-the dice roll to a stop and display number over it, shows little impact, make it bouncy and big and shake the screen slightly or something, put the number in a box maybe

\-the start walking and camera lerp are incredibly bad, it should zoom out a bit, fade in and out, have smooth non clipping animations, have cool animations for walking around others, show off the properties as you walk by

\-the UI of the card that pops up is garbage, multiple font sizes, multiple fonts, different weights, wall of text, important things are not emphasised, just appears doesn't slide in and wobble or anthing

\-clicking is just highlight, no real juice there once again

\-the coins and animation are ok, but very stilited and seem time consuming

\-the robber card is big and wall of irrelevant text again

\-the robber walks off the board, and the camera is bad again

\-going up and down the bridge sorta works, but just points out how its not smooth

\-the cowboys card is slightly better, but still a bad layout honestly

\-the ui elements look very AI generated

\-same animation/camera/walking issues as the others

\-they move 4 and I have no idea why, is it because one person rolled a 4? you aren't conveying that well

\-the interaction between two characters on the same square is barely there

replies.author: pennystudio
replies.body: Really appreciate you taking the time to give these valuable feedbacks. I can sorta visualize what you mean, now I will just have to spend some time polishing it. Thanks!

replies.author: fued
replies.body: yeah its all the little polish that takes 90% of the time in development. The core base gameplay is easy.

replies.author: pennystudio
replies.body: Funny thing is I actually enjoy polishing, which a lot of against better judgement of pushing the development along.

replies.author: fued
replies.body:
there is levels

1) get everything end to end working in a bare minimum state

2) polish it up as much as possible

3) add additional content to expend the minimum state now that you have a well built and polished core
